# Solution

We determine the values of $p$ for which the series

$$\sum_{n=N}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n\,(\log n)\,(\log\log n)\,\dotsm\,(\log_{j} n)\,(\log_{j+1} n)^{p}}$$

converges, where $\log_0 n = n$, $\log_{k+1} n = \log(\log_k n)$, and $N$ is large enough that all the iterated logarithms are positive and defined.

**Claim.** The series converges if and only if $p > 1$.

---

## Proof

We use the **integral test**. The summand

$$f(n) = \frac{1}{n\,(\log n)\,(\log\log n)\,\dotsm\,(\log_{j} n)\,(\log_{j+1} n)^{p}}$$

is positive and (for $n$ large enough) decreasing, so the series converges if and only if the improper integral

$$\int_{N}^{\infty} \frac{dx}{x\,(\log x)\,(\log\log x)\,\dotsm\,(\log_{j} x)\,(\log_{j+1} x)^{p}}$$

converges.

### Key substitution

Set $u = \log_{j+1} x$. Then, by the chain rule applied to the iterated logarithms,

$$du = \frac{dx}{x\,(\log x)\,(\log\log x)\,\dotsm\,(\log_{j} x)}.$$

Indeed, $\frac{d}{dx}\log x = \frac{1}{x}$, $\frac{d}{dx}\log\log x = \frac{1}{x\log x}$, and in general $\frac{d}{dx}\log_{k} x = \frac{1}{x\,(\log x)\,(\log\log x)\,\dotsm\,(\log_{k-1} x)}$. Composing these for $k = j+1$ gives exactly the displayed identity.

Therefore the integral transforms to

$$\int_{N}^{\infty} \frac{dx}{x\,(\log x)\,\dotsm\,(\log_{j} x)\,(\log_{j+1} x)^{p}} = \int_{\log_{j+1} N}^{\infty} \frac{du}{u^{p}}.$$

### Convergence of the transformed integral

The integral $\int_{a}^{\infty} u^{-p}\,du$ (with $a = \log_{j+1} N > 0$) is the standard $p$-integral:

- If $p > 1$: $\displaystyle\int_{a}^{\infty} u^{-p}\,du = \frac{a^{1-p}}{p-1} < \infty$, so it **converges**.
- If $p = 1$: $\displaystyle\int_{a}^{\infty} u^{-1}\,du = \lim_{b\to\infty}(\log b - \log a) = \infty$, so it **diverges**.
- If $p < 1$: $\displaystyle\int_{a}^{\infty} u^{-p}\,du = \lim_{b\to\infty}\frac{b^{1-p}}{1-p} = \infty$ (since $1-p>0$), so it **diverges**.

### Conclusion

By the integral test, the original series converges if and only if the transformed integral converges, which happens if and only if $p > 1$.

$$\boxed{\text{The series converges if and only if } p > 1.}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
